PACKET-08 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING
==========================================

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification of the work or author or a reading of these fragments. The only context I saw was a generic assistant setup (unrelated to these manuscripts). I listed the packet directory (ls) only to learn the image filenames. I did not open packet.json or any other directory, and I did not use the web.

Note: the scans carry modern pencil shelfmark labels (visible in the images themselves) reading approximately "Stams, STA, Fag. 81-1r", "Fag. 81-2r", "Fag. 81-3r", "Fag. 81-4r"(?), "Fag. 81-5r", "Fag. 81-6r". I use those only as fragment labels; they say nothing about the work.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of the whole mount)
-------------------------------------------------------
image-001 is a reduced overview of one photographic mount holding six separate parchment pieces on black card, with a colour checker (lower left) and a cm scale (right edge). Orientation: all pieces upright as mounted; text horizontal.
 - Upper left ("81-6r" label): a single leaf piece, ca. 10 x 12 cm, with one written block on its left half (in a small, fast, heavily abbreviated cursive in brown ink, red paraph strokes/touched letters), and the right half blank except for faint marks. The left edge of the written block is trimmed/faded so line beginnings are lost. A red "p 3"(?) mark at the top centre and a brown "p 3"(?) at the top right.
 - Upper centre ("81-3r" label): a small irregular scrap, holed and stained, with ~10 lines of a dark gothic book hand and a red ruling stroke near the bottom.
 - Upper right ("81-1r" label): a wide strip (ca. 14 x 11 cm) with three text columns of a regular gothic book hand (textura/semi-textura) in dark ink, red-ruled column bounds, red paraphs and red-touched capitals, and rubric-framed display lemmata (larger script inside red boxes). Between the left column and the middle column there is a wide blank margin carrying small marginal notes and numerals "1a", "2a", "3a", "4a"(?). This looks like it may be two adjacent pages of a bifolium (left column = outer column of one page, middle+right = the two columns of the next page), but that is a tentative interpretation.
 - Lower centre-left ("81-5r" label) and lower centre ("81-4r"(?) label): two narrow vertical strips in a small cursive book hand, brown ink, red touches; both cut at left and right so lines are fragmentary.
 - Lower right ("81-2r" label): a wide strip like 81-1r, same layout type: three columns, rubric-boxed display lemmata (e.g. "...ut autem" in large script at the bottom of the left column, "Sequit..."(?) large in the right column), red paraphs, blank inner margin.
Interpretation (tentative): 81-1r and 81-2r appear to be from the same manuscript (same hand, same layout): a running exposition in which short lemmata are set off in larger display script inside red boxes, followed by commentary prose in the normal text hand. 81-6r, 81-4r, 81-5r appear to be in a different, cursive hand. 81-3r is too small to judge.

CONVENTIONS: (x) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [box: ...] = text set inside a red-ruled box; [display: ...] = larger display script; ¶ = red paraph. Line numbers are counted from the top of the named image. Repeated lines in overlapping tiles are noted, not double counted. Columns are labelled A (left), B (middle), C (right) as they appear on each strip.
